title: Celebration: Life as a Dance
description: Religion has been made so serious. But the mystics laughed, and sang, and danced. Three monks who only laughed, a cracked pot that watered the flowers, children playing in a burning house, Chuang Tzu drumming and singing after his wife died, and a Zen master whose only miracle was eating when hungry. Then a meditation of dancing into silence.

beats.say: Go into any temple, any church, any mosque. Look at the faces. So serious. So sad. As if God is a strict headmaster, and life is an examination you are going to fail.
But look at a tree in spring. Look at a river after the rain. Look at a child on the first day of the holidays. Existence is not serious. It is celebrating.
The flowers are not working hard. The birds are not worried about tomorrow. They are simply here, singing.
Tonight, let us talk about the religion of joy. And at the end, let us dance.
In old China there were three monks who travelled from village to village. They never gave a sermon. They would simply stand in the middle of the market square... and start laughing.
Belly laughs. Tears running down their cheeks. And slowly the shopkeepers would come out, and the women at the well, and the children, and the whole village would start laughing with them.
Then the monks would move on to the next village. That was their whole teaching.
One day one of the three died. The villagers thought: now at last they will cry. But the other two danced and laughed around the body even more than before.
He has won, they said. He has gone first. We are laughing because he won the game.
And when the body was put on the fire, there was one more surprise. The dead monk had told his friends: don't change my clothes. And he had filled his pockets with fireworks.
Even his death was a joke. Even his death was a celebration. The whole village laughed until morning.
A water carrier in a village had two big pots hanging from a pole across his shoulders. One was perfect. The other had a long crack in it.
Every day he walked from the river to his master's house. The perfect pot arrived full. The cracked pot arrived half empty.
The cracked pot was ashamed. One day it spoke to the water carrier. I am sorry, it said. Because of my crack, all your hard work is wasted. You should throw me away.
The water carrier smiled. Tomorrow, he said, as we walk back, look at the side of the path.
The next day the pot looked. On its side of the path, all the way from the river to the house, there were beautiful wild flowers. On the other side, nothing. Only dust.
I knew about your crack, said the water carrier. So I planted seeds on your side. Every day you have been watering them. Without you, there would be no flowers on the master's table.
Your cracks are not your failure. Stop hiding them. Something is growing through them that the perfect ones will never know.
The Buddha told a story. A rich man had a big old house. One day, while he was outside, the house caught fire. And inside, his children were playing.
He shouted: come out, the house is burning! But the children were so busy with their toys that they did not listen. They did not even know what fire was.
So the father thought of a trick. He shouted: come out quickly, I have brought you new toys! Carts pulled by goats, carts pulled by deer! They are waiting at the gate!
The children came running out. And they were saved.
The world is the burning house, the Buddha said. Our worries, our greed, our quarrels are the fire. And we are the children, playing.
The masters say many things to get us out. Heaven, peace, enlightenment. These are the toys at the gate.
But what is really waiting outside is simply the open sky. And the joy of being alive under it.
When Chuang Tzu's wife died, his old friend Hui Tzu came to offer his sympathy. And he found Chuang Tzu sitting on the floor, beating on a pot like a drum, and singing.
Hui Tzu was shocked. She lived with you, she brought up your children, she grew old with you. Not to weep is bad enough. But to sing? This is too much!

Chuang Tzu said: when she died, I grieved like anyone. But then I looked back to before she was born. There was no life, no body, not even breath. Then, out of the great mystery, there was breath, and a body, and life.
Now there has been another change, and she has gone back. Like spring becoming summer, autumn becoming winter. She is resting now in the great house of heaven and earth.
If I went on sobbing and wailing, it would show that I understand nothing. So I stopped. And I sing.
Celebration is not ignoring death. It is seeing life so deeply that even death becomes a part of the dance.
The Zen master Bankei was giving a talk to a crowd of farmers, when a priest from another sect pushed his way to the front. Our founder could do miracles, he boasted. What miracles can you do?
He could stand on one side of the river, holding a brush, and his disciple on the other side holding paper, and he could write a holy name across the water in the air!
Bankei smiled. Perhaps your fox can do that trick, he said. But that is not the way of Zen.
My miracle is this. When I am hungry, I eat. When I am thirsty, I drink. When I am tired, I sleep.
It sounds so simple. But try it. When you eat, you are reading the newspaper. When you sleep, you are planning tomorrow. When you walk, you are somewhere else.
The priest went away angry. But the farmers stayed. They understood Bankei better than any scholar, because they lived close to the earth, eating when hungry, sleeping when tired.
To be totally where you are, doing what you are doing... that is the real miracle. And it is available to you every single moment.
So celebration does not mean that you must have a festival every day. It means bringing a festive heart to ordinary things.
Cooking the rice as if you are cooking for a guest you love. Sweeping the floor as if it were a dance. Saying good morning to the milkman as if you mean it.
Seriousness is a disease of the ego. It wants to be important. Joy is the health of the soul. It does not care about being important at all.
Laugh more. Sing in the bathroom. Dance in the kitchen when nobody is looking. Be a little foolish. The wise ones always were.
Look at the old women in the villages at harvest time, singing while they cut the wheat. The work is hard, the sun is hot. And still they sing.
They have not read any books about celebration. They simply know that a song makes the field lighter.
Existence is dancing all around you. Join in.
Now let us end the way we began. Stand up, if you can. Let the body loosen. And close your eyes.
Begin to move. Any way the body wants. Sway, shake, bend, turn. Don't make a dance. Let the dance make you.
Let the joy come up from the belly. If you feel like laughing, laugh. If you feel like jumping, jump. Nobody is watching.
Become the dance so totally that there is no dancer left. Only dancing.
And now... stop. Freeze wherever you are. Completely still. Feel the energy still dancing inside the stillness.
Now sit, or lie down. Let everything settle, like dust after a festival procession has passed.
The silence after the dance is very deep. Very alive. Rest in it. You don't have to do anything now.
And when you are ready, open your eyes. Take this dance with you into your day. Thank you, my friend. Celebrate.
